quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: Why should a load be placed low on a motorcycle?

options.text: A high load raises the motorcycle's center of gravity.
A high load may block the turn signals.
You may not be able to see over a high load.
Others cannot see a low load.

questions.correctAnswerText: A high load raises the motorcycle's center of gravity.
questions.explanation: A high load raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and makes the bike less stable.

questions.question: The front brake provides about how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?

options.text: About 25 percent
About 50 percent
About 70 percent
About 95 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger in a sidecar, you should:

options.text: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
Start slowing down later than usual.
Brake hard to stop quickly.
Brake gently to avoid overworking the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
questions.explanation: The extra weight of a passenger makes your motorcycle harder to handle. Your motorcycle will need more distance to stop.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Downshift.
Speed up.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
Slowly apply the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up because this makes the wobble worse. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly, slow down by gradually closing the throttle, lean forward and down, and pull off the road when safe. Do not brake, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: To reduce your chance of an accident, you should:

options.text: Ride only in the afternoon.
Follow other vehicles very closely.
Look only at your controls, not ahead.
Signal your intentions to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal your intentions to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To reduce crashes, make yourself visible to others. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and constantly watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: When carrying a load in a sidecar, you should:

options.text: Let the load move freely.
Secure the load so it does not shift.
Place the load loosely in the seat.
Secure the load at the front of the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the load so it does not shift.
questions.explanation: Secure your load so it cannot move and affect how the motorcycle handles. Place the load toward the back of the sidecar to prevent the nose from tipping up during sharp left turns.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should be worn:

options.text: Never.
Only during the day.
Only at night.
Day and night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Day and night.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight. Wearing bright colors and reflective clothing at all times makes you more visible.

questions.question: A major effect of alcohol is:

options.text: Better riding ability.
Slowed body functions.
More nervousness.
More alertness.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowed body functions.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows down both physical and mental functions.

questions.question: Crashes are most likely to happen to:

options.text: Experienced riders.
Beginning riders.
Riders familiar with their motorcycle.
Riders who completed a safety course.

questions.correctAnswerText: Beginning riders.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen most often to untrained, beginning riders who do not know their motorcycle well.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Ride slower than usual.
Follow other vehicles more closely than you would alone.
Ride faster than usual.
Brake a little later than you would if riding alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than usual.
questions.explanation: The extra weight of a passenger means your motorcycle takes longer to speed up, slow down, and turn. Reduce your speed, start slowing earlier, increase your following distance, and look for larger gaps in traffic when crossing or merging.

questions.question: What happens to your steering if your front tire goes flat while riding?

options.text: The steering will feel heavy.
The steering will feel loose.
There will be no change in the steering.
The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The steering will feel heavy.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes steering feel heavy. If your steering feels heavy, pull off the road and check your tires right away.

questions.question: If you can't avoid a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: If you must ride on a slippery surface, keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible.

questions.question: A small animal enters your lane while you are riding in traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Swerve into other lanes if needed to avoid hitting the animal.
Switch lanes as quickly as possible.
Stay in your lane.
Flash your lights to scare the animal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in your lane to avoid hitting other vehicles. While you should avoid hitting an animal when possible, swerving into traffic is more dangerous. A small animal is less dangerous than a collision with another vehicle.

questions.question: How do headache, cold, and hay fever medications usually affect you?

options.text: They make you drowsy.
They make you more alert.
They make you hungry.
They make you unable to concentrate.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: Most medications for headaches, colds, hay fever, allergies, and nerves can make you drowsy. This can affect your ability to ride safely. Know how any medication affects you before riding.

questions.question: What blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is the legal limit for intoxication?

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.08 percent
0.1 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: In Kentucky, 0.08 percent BAC is the legal limit for intoxication. Riding a motorcycle while under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Your rear wheel locks while braking on a good road surface. What should you do?

options.text: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then quickly re-apply it.
Release the rear brake and downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop. Your motorcycle can still be controlled with a locked rear wheel if it stays upright and travels straight.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's braking power comes from the front brake?

options.text: Less than half
About 70 percent
Only when the roadway is wet
All of the braking power

questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is much stronger than the rear brake and provides about 70 percent of your motorcycle's total stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Why is riding next to another rider a problem?

options.text: It limits the space you can use on the road.
It limits your escape routes if something goes wrong.
It makes communication easier.
It makes it easier for cars to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It limits your escape routes if something goes wrong.
questions.explanation: Do not ride alongside another motorcycle because it reduces your options to escape if a hazard appears.

questions.question: How do you lean your motorcycle to turn?

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.
Apply the front brake.
Apply the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To lean your motorcycle for a turn, press on the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.

questions.question: How is passing on a motorcycle different from passing in a car?

options.text: Visibility is more important on a motorcycle.
Visibility is less important on a motorcycle.
You should pass on the shoulder instead of the main road.
You must make eye contact with the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Visibility is more important on a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Visibility is more critical when riding a motorcycle. Motorcycles are smaller and can easily disappear into a driver's blind spot. Other drivers may not notice you even if they look.
